CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right leg pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 43-year-old female who injured her right leg while bowling. She was running up to the lane with her bowling ball when she swung it forward and struck her right leg with the ball instead of releasing it down the lane. She fell as a result of the injury. She reports minimal swelling but some bruising on the posterior aspect of the leg. She is able to walk only with great difficulty and describes the leg as very sore with ambulation. She would avoid stairs at all costs. She is currently taking ibuprofen and acetaminophen alternately for pain management. On examination, there is significant tenderness to the lateral aspect of the right upper leg. She does not have pain or tenderness with flexion or extension of the lower leg.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atopic eczema. Previous colectomy for diverticulitis (patient had diverticulosis that progressed to diverticulitis requiring partial colectomy).

MEDICATIONS
Fluocinonide for eczema as needed when itchy. Ibuprofen and acetaminophen alternating for current leg pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Significant tenderness to lateral aspect of right upper leg. No pain or tenderness with flexion or extension of lower leg. X-ray of femur shows normal anatomy with no evidence of fracture or swelling.

RESULTS
Right femur X-ray: Normal, no fracture, no swelling.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Contusion of right leg. Started on mobic 15 mg once daily as anti-inflammatory. Patient instructed to use ice for pain. Expected improvement in approximately one week. Patient to return if symptoms do not improve.
